text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- No breakthrough at summit.
- U.S. congressmen: Block Palestinian Authority aid over land-sale death penalty.
- Ultra-Orthodox Jewish Shas party weekly drops tobacco advertisements.
- Israeli Treasury gives local authorities OK for property tax rises.
- Swiss retailer Manor AG denies aborting Israel plans due to political risk.
- Israel Corporation president Erwin Eisenberg: No compromise on will.
- Koor first-quarter net slightly down.
- Ofer-Wertheim to up its UMB holding to 51 percent.
GLOBES
- Bank of Israel estimates: No more than a quarter of foreign currency balances will leave the country after liberalisation.
HAARETZ
- Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa: Progress depends on an Israeli concession.
- Government committee recommends issuing El Al shares on stock exchange and allow the airline to fly on sabbaths.
- Former Supreme Court President Meir Shamgar says written constitution the most effective tool to ensure basic rights.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Labour leader Shimon Peres are biggest moonlighters in parliament.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israel: "We're betting on Mubarak as 'the peace engine'".
- Israel's Tadiran company will reduce workforce by 150 by year's end, director-general says.
MAARIV
- No breakthrough, no breakdown at summit. Israel: Progress. Palestinians: Disappointment. Egypt: It's a start.
- Pioneer in Israeli broadcasting, Yoram Ronen, dead at age of 64 after long and difficult illness.
